bib.title: Think Bayes, ch. 8: Observer bias
bib.venue: book chapter (Think Bayes, 1st ed., Green Tea Press / O'Reilly, 2012; no journal)

question: How does a length-biased sample (the Red Line wait) change the prior, and how is a posterior over elapsed time and arrival rate turned into a wait-time prediction and a stop-or-taxi decision?

results.claim: A passenger arriving at random sees gaps oversampled in proportion to their length: with 5 and 10 minute gaps equally likely, the true mean is 7.5 and the observed mean 8.33.
results.setup: gaps of 5 or 10 minutes with equal probability
results.quote: the average time between trains, as seen by an arriving passenger, is 8.33 minutes

results.claim: On collected Red Line data the mean of z is 7.8 minutes, of zb 8.8 (about 13% higher) and of y 4.4.
results.setup: south-bound Kendall Square arrivals, 4 to 6 pm, 5 weekdays, about 15 arrivals a day
results.quote: The mean of z is 7.8 minutes

results.claim: After seeing 15 passengers at lam 2 per minute, the next train is expected within 5 minutes with about 80% confidence.
results.setup: Poisson likelihood of k arrivals in x minutes; lam known

results.claim: Five days of data give 36 arrivals over about 18 minutes, so lam is about 2 passengers per minute.
results.setup: five (k1, y, k2) tuples; grid 0 to 5 per minute, 51 points
results.quote: so you would estimate that the arrival rate is 2 passengers per minute

results.claim: Including uncertainty in lam gives a result very similar to a point estimate, because the response is approximately linear.
Accepting a 10% chance of missing the connection, wait while there are fewer than 30 passengers and take a taxi above that.
results.setup: P(y>15 min) vs platform count; three 30 to 50 minute delays a year added by hand
results.quote: we should stay and wait as long as there are fewer than 30 passen

limits: Rate assumed constant across days and no special events; the long-delay frequency (3 a year) is from memory, not data; distribution of z assumed known; WaitTimeCalculator code in the text has a pmf/pmf_z naming slip.
practices: Treat observations as a length-biased sample and unbias before modelling (p.83).
Handle an uncertain input by running the analysis per value and mixing with posterior weights (p.91-92).
Include input variability when the system response is non-linear (p.92).

terms.definition: values from the actual distribution are oversampled in proportion to their value
